passages.title: The Whispering Trees
passages.text: Long ago, the trees of the forest could speak, but only to people who were patient enough to listen. A young woodcutter named Edwin often sat beneath an old oak to eat his lunch. One day, he heard a faint voice warning him that a storm was coming. Although the sky was clear, Edwin decided to trust the tree and hurried home. That night, a terrible storm destroyed half of the village's fields, but Edwin had already brought his goats inside. From then on, the villagers stopped laughing at him for talking to trees.

passages.title: Forest Schools
passages.text: Forest schools are becoming popular in the UK. Children spend at least one day a week outdoors, whatever the weather, building shelters, identifying plants and learning to work in teams. Teachers say that pupils who struggle in the classroom often do well outside, and many become more confident. However, some parents worry about safety and the cost of waterproof clothing.

passages.title: Review: Moonlight Mushroom Café
passages.text: The setting is magical: tables among glowing mushrooms and fairy lights. The staff were friendly, although our food took nearly an hour to arrive. The berry pie was delicious, but the soup was cold and rather salty. It's worth visiting for the atmosphere, but I'd recommend booking ahead and going on a weekday when it's quieter.

passages.title: Gina's Diary
passages.text: I've always been scared of heights, so when my friends suggested the treetop adventure trail, I nearly said no. In the end I went, mainly because I didn't want to be the only one left behind. The first bridge was terrifying and my legs were shaking. But by the third platform, I was actually enjoying the view. I'm not saying I've completely got over my fear, but I'm proud I didn't give up.

passages.title: Make a Bird Feeder
passages.text: First, tie a piece of string around a pine cone. Next, spread peanut butter all over it — if anyone in your house has a nut allergy, use vegetable fat instead. Then roll the cone in birdseed until it's completely covered. Finally, hang it from a branch that cats can't reach. Remember to keep it filled during winter, when food is hardest for birds to find.

passages.title: The Lantern Makers
passages.text: Every autumn, the families of Willowmere make paper lanterns for the Festival of Light. The tradition began two hundred years ago, when a lost child was guided home by a line of lanterns hung along the river. Today, around three hundred lanterns are made each year. Children decorate them with drawings of animals, while adults fix the frames, which are made of thin bamboo. Although electric lights would be easier and safer, most villagers insist on real candles, saying that 'a lantern without a flame is just a paper bag'.

passages.title: Ask Aunt Bramble
passages.text: Dear Aunt Bramble, my best friend has started spending all her time with a new girl in our class. I feel left out, but I don't want to seem jealous. What should I do? — Lonely Leaf. Dear Lonely Leaf, it's natural to feel hurt. Rather than staying silent, tell your friend calmly how you feel, without blaming her. You could also suggest doing something together, all three of you. You might discover that you like the new girl too. And remember, it's healthy to have more than one close friend.
